clue.text: Barrie's flighty young hero isn't at home…

definitions.text: Barrie's flighty young hero isn't at home…

parts.words: Barrie's flighty young hero isn't at home
parts.note: J M Barrie's flying boy is Peter Pan; saying that he is out of the house, contracted with an apostrophe, gives a phrase meaning dwindles away

explanation.surface: A note that the boy who never grew up has flown off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Peter's out' (Peter is not at home) as one phrasal verb meaning gradually fades or comes to an end; the ellipsis carries the sense on to the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase describes something dwindling to nothing, as a stream or an effort gradually fails.

clue.text: Diplomatic messenger loses nothing but it's a deadly sin

indicators.note: the messenger word loses a letter, so something is taken out of it

parts.note: an envoy is a diplomat sent with a message
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An ambassador who gives up everything, yet still commits a cardinal sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' takes the O (nothing) out of ENVOY.
explanation.definitionFit: Covetousness of another's good fortune is one of the seven deadly sins.

clue.text: Hard-wearing coats achieved by mixing men's ale

indicators.note: mixing the letters stirs them together into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the apostrophe giving no letter

explanation.surface: Durable paint finishes produced by blending beer for the lads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by mixing' rearranges MENS and ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Enamels are glossy, tough layers of paint or glaze applied as protective coverings.

clue.text: Everything in shop for use by light craftsmen

indicators.note: one word placed in another, so it goes inside

explanation.surface: A whole workshop stocked for delicate artisans.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'craftsmen': not artisans but people who sail light craft, small boats, which is what this vessel is.
explanation.definitionFit: A shallop is a light open boat, the kind used by those who handle small sailing vessels.

clue.text: In four generations the yearning that has been concealed

indicators.note: the letters sit in the clue words, running across the gap between them

explanation.surface: A longing kept secret across four generations of a family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' and 'that has been concealed' both point to the run hidden in fOUR GEnerations.
explanation.definitionFit: An urge is a strong desire or longing.

clue.text: Advice to the poultry rustler: make a dash for it

definitions.meaning: a chicken thief should force entry into the hens' pen, which is called a run

explanation.surface: A tip for a hen thief: flee quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'run' is an enclosure for chickens, so breaking in is what a poultry thief does.
explanation.definitionFit: Both readings: forcing entry into a hen enclosure, and suddenly starting to sprint.

clue.text: Artist in choir could reform the actor's craft

indicators.note: to reform letters is to shape them into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A painter singing with a choral group might reshape theatrical skill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could reform' rearranges the thirteen letters of ARTIST IN CHOIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic means theatrical, so this phrase names the skill of acting on stage.

clue.text: What every second-hand car buyer hopes to do

definitions.text: What every second-hand car buyer hopes to do

parts.words: What every second-hand car buyer hopes to do
parts.note: the motoring setting points to steering a vehicle, but the phrase means getting a low price by haggling

explanation.surface: Someone buying a used vehicle hopes for a test run and a cheap deal.
explanation.walkthrough: The car buyer suggests 'drive' in the motoring sense; the idiom means to haggle hard for a good deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain shrewdly and secure favourable terms is the idiom, with a play on the car being driven.

clue.text: Old statesman was happy with fourteen pounds

parts.note: a stone is a British unit of weight equal to fourteen pounds

explanation.surface: A former politician was pleased with his weight.
explanation.walkthrough: William Gladstone was a Victorian British Prime Minister; a stone (14 lb) is still used in Britain for body weight.
explanation.definitionFit: Gladstone was four times Prime Minister of Britain in the nineteenth century.

clue.text: Short race arranged for bandsmen

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, as music is arranged for a band

explanation.surface: A sprint organised for members of the band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arranged' rearranges the letters of SHORT RACE.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestra is a body of musicians playing together.

clue.text: Bread of idleness?

definitions.meaning: a shaped mass of baked dough
the noun stands for the verb meaning to laze about

explanation.surface: Asking what food a lazy person eats.
explanation.walkthrough: One word is both a baked shape of bread and a verb for lounging about doing nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A baker's single shaped bake, and also a verb for lazing around.

clue.text: Beauty produces a ring for the ear

indicators.note: something meant for the ear is heard, not seen, so the word sounds like another

parts.note: a bell is something that rings, a ring on the telephone

explanation.surface: A lovely woman's voice rings out pleasantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for the ear' says BELL is heard as BELLE, a French-derived word for a beautiful woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired at a gathering.

clue.text: Commonly where the prisoners are to cause a commotion

definitions.meaning: in common slang the word means a prison
to ... things up is to create a disturbance

explanation.surface: A riot breaking out in a jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Commonly' marks slang: 'in stir' means in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for a jail, and a verb for rousing trouble or agitation.

clue.text: Smooth going north and south

indicators.note: in a down entry, reading the same going up the grid and going down it means a palindrome

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A flat road running in both directions.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down light the word reads the same upwards (north) and downwards (south).
explanation.definitionFit: Level means flat and even, with no bumps.

clue.text: Provisional financial receipt for the pilgrim's pouch

definitions.meaning: a certificate issued for shares before the full documents
an old word for a small bag carried by pilgrims

explanation.surface: Paperwork kept in a traveller's satchel.
explanation.definitionFit: A temporary certificate for stock or money, and an archaic word for a wayfarer's satchel.

clue.text: Clubs for motorists

definitions.meaning: golf clubs with large heads used for long shots

explanation.surface: Associations for car owners, like the AA.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clubs' looks like societies; here they are golf woods for teeing off.
explanation.definitionFit: Golfers' long-hitting woods, and people at the wheel of a car.

clue.text: Hungry like a bird?

definitions.meaning: a bird pecks, so the word read as peck plus -ish suggests bird-like

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone famished resembles a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the second reading: the suffix -ish means 'like', so 'peck-ish' is bird-like.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling a little hungry, and, split up, resembling something that pecks.

clue.text: Ragged garb for lace-makers

definitions.meaning: people who make tatting, a knotted lace, are called by this name

explanation.surface: Lace workers dressed in shabby clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatting is a handmade knotted lace; those who make it tat.
explanation.definitionFit: Torn rags of clothing, and people who make knotted lace by hand.

clue.text: Taverns could be the making of such a domestic employee

indicators.note: the letters of the word could be made into another word by rearranging them

explanation.surface: Working in pubs could build character for a household helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could be the making of' rearranges TAVERNS.
explanation.definitionFit: A servant is someone employed to work in a household.

clue.text: Short day finishes off companions

parts.note: Fri is the short form of Friday

explanation.surface: An early end to Friday sees off one's mates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Friends are close companions.

clue.text: Who establishes an institution to sink a ship?

definitions.meaning: a person who sets up a college or charity
a ship that fills with water and goes down

explanation.surface: Asking whether the creator of an institute would wreck a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who sets up an organisation, and a verb for a vessel going down.

clue.text: Parsimonious, or not far from it

definitions.meaning: mean with money, an old sense of the word

explanation.surface: Someone is stingy, or close to being so.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy in an old sense, and close in distance.

clue.text: Classical guardian who takes sugar immoderately

indicators.note: without moderation, the letters are thrown about wildly

explanation.surface: A mythic watchman with a sweet tooth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'immoderately' rearranges SUGAR. Argus was the hundred-eyed giant set to guard Io in Greek myth.
explanation.definitionFit: Argus Panoptes was the many-eyed watchman of Greek mythology.

clue.text: S. scarcity in the country leaves its mark

indicators.note: out in the country, away from the town, the urban place leaves the word

explanation.surface: A rural shortage leaves a lasting impression.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the country leaves' removes CITY (the country being the opposite of the city) from SCARCITY.
explanation.definitionFit: A scar is a mark left on the skin after a wound heals.

clue.text: The colour of the spendthrift's money

definitions.text: The colour of the spendthrift's money

parts.words: The colour of the spendthrift's money
parts.note: a colour word that is also British slang for squandering money

explanation.surface: Asking what hue a wasteful person's cash is.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang to 'blue' money is to spend it recklessly.
explanation.definitionFit: A primary colour, and the slang verb for frittering away cash.

clue.text: The metricationists would have us abolish these appendages

definitions.text: The metricationists would have us abolish these appendages

parts.words: The metricationists would have us abolish these appendages
parts.note: metric reformers want to drop an imperial length unit that is also the name of body parts

explanation.surface: Campaigners for metric units want to cut off our limbs.
explanation.walkthrough: Britain's metric campaigners wanted imperial units such as the twelve-inch measure replaced by metres.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperial units of twelve inches share the name of the parts we stand on.

clue.text: Those beastly Stock Exchange characters!

parts.note: market traders who expect prices to rise or fall are named after two animals

explanation.surface: An exclamation at nasty City traders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beastly' means unpleasant on the surface, but literally refers to animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Market optimists and pessimists are named after two animals, hence beastly.

clue.text: No sinister quality required by ones right-hand man

definitions.text: No sinister quality required by ones right-hand man

parts.words: No sinister quality required by ones right-hand man
parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, and its opposite, right, gives the word for skill

explanation.surface: A trusted assistant must have nothing evil about him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' means left in Latin; the answer comes from Latin dexter, right, so a right-hand man needs right-handedness, i.e. skill.
explanation.definitionFit: Skill with the hands, from the Latin word for right-handed.
